title: An Execution Petition under Order XXI Rule 11 CPC is the procedural instrument by which a Decree-Holder enforces a civil court decree

content.overview: An Execution Petition under Order XXI Rule 11 CPC is the procedural instrument by which a Decree-Holder enforces a civil court decree. Sub-rule (2) mandates a strict 10-column tabular application detailing the decree, payments, appeals, costs, and the specific mode of execution under Section 51 CPC.
content.short: An Execution Petition under Order XXI Rule 11 CPC is the procedural instrument by which a Decree-Holder enforces a civil court decree. Sub-rule (2) mandates a strict 10-column tabular application detailing the decree, payments, appeals, costs, and the specific mode of execution under Section 51 CPC.
content.detailed:
Core Drafting Skeleton & Mandatory Table under Order XXI Rule 11(2) CPC

1. Cause Title & Executing Court
   • IN THE COURT OF THE CIVIL JUDGE / DISTRICT JUDGE AT [Station]
   • Execution Petition No. … of 20…
   • In Original Suit No. … of 20…
   • [Decree-Holder Name] … Decree-Holder (D.H.) vs. [Judgment-Debtor Name] … Judgment-Debtor (J.D.)
   • "APPLICATION FOR EXECUTION UNDER ORDER XXI RULE 11(2) READ WITH SECTION 51 CPC"

2. The Mandatory 10-Column Tabular Statement (Order XXI Rule 11(2))
   • Column 1: Number of the suit (e.g., O.S. No. 102/2021).
   • Column 2: Names of parties (Full particulars of D.H. and J.D.).
   • Column 3: Date of the decree (e.g., Decreed on 15.03.2023).
   • Column 4: Whether any appeal has been preferred against the decree (e.g., "No appeal has been filed; decree has attained finality" or "First Appeal No. … was dismissed on …").
   • Column 5: Whether any, and (if any) what, payment or adjustment has been made between the parties (e.g., "None; zero payment received").
   • Column 6: Whether any previous applications have been made for execution, their dates and results (e.g., "None; this is the first execution application").
   • Column 7: Amount of debt or damages with interest awarded by the decree, or other relief granted (Principal sum Rs. … + Interest @ …% per annum from … to date of application = Total Rs. …).
   • Column 8: Amount of costs awarded in the decree (e.g., Rs. … as per decree sheet).
   • Column 9: Name of the person against whom execution is sought (Name and description of J.D. No. 1 and 2).
   • Column 10: Mode in which the assistance of the Court is required (as per Section 51 CPC):
     (a) By attachment and sale of the movable/immovable properties of the J.D. detailed in Schedule-A annexed hereto (Order XXI Rules 43, 54);
     (b) By arrest and detention of the J.D. in civil prison (subject to Section 51 proviso & Section 56 CPC);
     (c) By delivery of possession of the suit property described in Schedule-B (Order XXI Rule 35);
     (d) By appointment of a Receiver under Order XL CPC.

3. Verification Clause & Supporting Affidavit
   • Verification by the Decree-Holder under Order XXI Rule 11(2) confirming that the particulars in Columns 1–10 are true and correct to the best of their knowledge.

Critical Practice & Statutory Directives:
• Section 47 CPC: All questions relating to execution, discharge, or satisfaction of the decree must be determined by the executing court and never by a fresh independent suit.
• Section 56 CPC: Absolute statutory bar prohibiting arrest or detention of women in execution of a money decree.
• Section 51 Proviso: Arrest and civil imprisonment cannot be ordered for mere poverty or inability to pay; the court must record reasons that the debtor has current means to pay and is willfully refusing, or has fraudulently transferred property (Jolly George Varghese).
• Limitation Periods (Limitation Act, 1963):
  - Article 136: 12 years for executing any decree or order of a civil court.
  - Article 135: 3 years for mandatory injunction decrees.
• Order XXI Rule 22: Mandatory show-cause notice to judgment debtor if execution is filed more than 2 years after the date of the decree.
• Rahul S. Shah Guidelines (2021): Supreme Court directed executing courts to conclude proceedings within 6 months and curtail frivolous delaying objections.

cases.name: Rahul S. Shah v. Jinendra Kumar Gandhi
cases.holding: Laid down mandatory procedural directions for executing courts nationwide, directing that execution proceedings must be completed within 6 months and frivolous obstruction by judgment-debtors must be dealt with by police assistance and heavy costs.
cases.relevance: Benchmark Supreme Court charter on speedy civil execution and elimination of procedural delay.

cases.name: Jolly George Varghese v. Bank of Cochin
cases.holding: Under Section 51 CPC read with Article 21 and Article 11 of the ICCPR, a judgment debtor cannot be imprisoned merely for poverty or honest inability to pay a civil money decree; there must be bad faith or contumacious refusal to pay.
cases.relevance: Human rights and constitutional restraints on civil arrest and detention.

cases.name: Babu Lal v. Hazari Lal Kishori Lal
cases.holding: The executing court has plenary jurisdiction to grant actual possession of property in execution of a decree for specific performance under Section 28(3) of the Specific Relief Act.
cases.relevance: Scope of executing court powers in specific performance decrees.

bareActPointers: Order XXI Rule 11(2) CPC (10-column written execution application)
Section 51 CPC (Modes of execution: attachment, arrest, receiver, delivery)
Section 47 CPC (Executing court alone to decide execution questions)
Section 56 CPC (Prohibition of arrest of women in money decrees)
Order XXI Rule 22 CPC (Notice after 2 years)
examTips: Order XXI is the longest Order in the CPC with 106 Rules.
Under Section 56 CPC, women can never be arrested or detained in civil prison for execution of a money decree.
Notice under Order XXI Rule 22 is mandatory if the execution petition is filed after 2 years from the date of the decree.
Under Article 136 of the Limitation Act, 1963, limitation for executing a civil decree is 12 years (except mandatory injunction which is 3 years under Article 135).
